questions.question: What are the most effective safety restraints in a traffic crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and reduce serious injury. Airbags work with safety belts to protect you in front-end crashes. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: They are better drivers because they are not hungry.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This makes it hard to stay in your lane and control your vehicle.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You have your emergency brake on.
You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Your brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Always keep your brake lights working when driving on any road.

questions.question: What must you do when you leave your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, as long as an approaching train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.
Yes, if you first look carefully in both directions.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: What can impair a person's ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and being tired can all impair your driving ability.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Then quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: Is smoking while driving a distracting activity?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving abilities.
No, it helps drivers stay alert.
Yes, it is a distracting activity.
No, it is not a distracting activity.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a distracting activity.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is dangerous. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: Who has the right-of-way when a funeral procession is present?
questions.explanation: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. When the first vehicle enters an intersection, all other vehicles in the procession can follow through, even if the light is red.

questions.question: What helps a person recover from drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will allow alcohol's effects to wear off.

questions.question: When should you signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from the curb?

options.text: Only if other vehicles are nearby.
It is a good habit and the law requires it.
Only during the move, not before.
Not necessary if you drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Always signal before pulling away from the curb so other drivers know your plans.

questions.question: What is the purpose of road markings on highways?

options.text: They are only used in construction areas.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.explanation: Road markings help drivers stay in the correct lane, show safe passing zones, and warn about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent drowsiness on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest at regular times.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest at regular times.
questions.explanation: Take regular breaks on long trips. Get out, rest, and stretch even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: When turning left, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, bicyclists, and any other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots regularly.
Drivers giving the right-of-way to others.
Drivers keeping a four-second distance behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for conditions. Always drive at or below the speed limit and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid getting tired on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Alternate feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Take a break every two hours on long trips. If you get drowsy, pull over safely and take a nap or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean you must stop and wait for the right-of-way. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.explanation: Stop signs are eight-sided. This shape means you must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on a downhill slope than smaller vehicles.
Need a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on an uphill slope than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are large and heavy. They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm. Slow down and let the aggressive driver pass. Do not make eye contact or make gestures. Put distance between your vehicle and theirs.

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause a crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign tells you to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop and let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Night driving is more difficult than daytime driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as well in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Increase how far you need to stop.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase your stopping distance and make turning harder. They also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, you should use ____ to show that you are turning.
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers you are turning.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other traffic is visible.
Signal only if other traffic is visible.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other traffic is visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Make it a habit so you never forget.
